lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- Fluency Under Pressure
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ana Paula Teodoro Valdivia | Lesson 8 -- Fluency Under Pressure

listenings.text: I run teams in eight countries, and I am on calls in English with people from most of them. Let me tell you what I notice, and what I do not notice. I do not notice when somebody is searching for a word. Honestly, I do not. Everybody searches for words, including me, and English is my first language. What I notice is silence with no explanation. When a person goes quiet for six or seven seconds and says nothing at all, I have no idea what is happening. Are you thinking? Do you disagree with me? Did your connection drop? I start guessing, and my guesses are usually wrong. So here is the phrase I respect most on a call: bear with me. Three words, and suddenly the silence is not a problem, it is a pause. Take ten seconds. Take twenty. I will wait, because now I know what the silence means. And here is the one thing I do not forgive: a confident guess. If you do not know, tell me you will get back to me. I can work with that. I cannot work with a number that somebody invented to fill the gap.

I want to tell you about the worst thirty seconds of my professional life, and they were very quiet ones. I was on a call with a client, in English, and he asked me about a filing deadline in a country I had never worked in. I did not know the answer. And instead of saying that, I was embarrassed, so I said a number. I gave him a date. I said it confidently, the way people do when they are trying to sound like they know. Three weeks later that date was in a plan, in a budget, and in an email to a regulator. It was wrong by eleven days, and fixing it cost more than my fee for the whole matter. Nobody shouted at me. That was almost worse. So now I have five sentences written on a piece of paper stuck to my monitor. Give me a second. Let me double-check that. I will get back to you today. Do you mean the filing date, or the payment date? Bear with me. And here is the strange part. I almost never use them. Just knowing they are there took the panic away.

extra_audio.text: Bear with me for a second, I want to get this right. Just to confirm, do you mean the master agreement, or the local one? Off the top of my head, the notice period there is thirty days. Let me double-check that and I will get back to you before the end of the day.
